capabilities: Edit diagram code blocks on a canvas and write the layout back as plain text
Render 12 diagram types (mind map, flowchart, sequence, ER, Gantt and more) with a local SVG renderer
Edit Markdown tables in a spreadsheet-style editor with sum, avg and arithmetic formulas
Provide a customizable formatting toolbar with format painter, colors and 15 text batch tools
Manage attachment folder templates, rename orphans and hide or manually sort file explorer entries
disambiguation: Despite the toolkit name, the centerpiece is visual editing of diagram code blocks; the toolbar, file-browser and attachment features are optional side modules.
extras: The attachment management, file hiding and manual file sorting modules are disabled by default and must be turned on in settings; all rendering is local with no network requests, no accounts and no paid features; BRAT is supported for beta installs.
motivation: The author wanted diagrams and tables to stay as plain text inside notes so they remain editable, versionable with Git and readable by other Markdown tools, instead of being exported as images.
problem: Diagrams in Obsidian are usually pasted as screenshots or exported attachments that can no longer be edited together with the note text, and Markdown tables have no spreadsheet-like editing with formulas.
